scenario: Returning a faulty item at a shop
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Pulaar

dialogue.speaker: Customer
dialogue.text: Miɗo naate miɗo fii maɗa woɗɗo yitere, mi beɓe ɓe yitere.
dialogue.translation: Yesterday I bought this thing from your shop, but it’s broken. I want you to replace it.

dialogue.speaker: Shopkeeper
dialogue.text: Hule woɗɗo ɗum ɓe yitere? Miɗo yitere ngurni.
dialogue.translation: Is this thing really broken? That’s a problem.

dialogue.speaker: Customer
dialogue.text: Eey! Miɗo naate miɗo woɗɗo fii maɗa, miɗo yitere ngurni.
dialogue.translation: Yes! I bought this thing here yesterday, and now I have a problem.

dialogue.speaker: Shopkeeper
dialogue.text: Miɗo beɓe miɗo woɗɗo maɓɓe. Jooni, miɗo beɓe miɗo woɗɗo hule.
dialogue.translation: I can give you another one. Now, I’ll give you another one again.

dialogue.speaker: Customer
dialogue.text: Jiyaa! Amɗa woɗɗo makko miɗo beɓe. No miɗo beɓe hule.
dialogue.translation: Thank you! Give me my money back first. And then give me another one.

dialogue.speaker: Shopkeeper
dialogue.text: Miɗo beɓe woɗɗo maɓɓe, miɗo naate naange. Miɗo beɓe woɗɗo makko ammaa woɗɗo maɓɓe.
dialogue.translation: I’ll give you another one, I promise. I’ll give you your money back, but first take this other one.

key_phrases.translation: I will give you another one.

dialogue.text: Saba dow leɗɗe wuro, wonaa heɗɗo muu you worse?
dialogue.translation: For five years of work, are you able to do anything else?

key_phrases.phrase: Hoy, leɗɗe waɗa muu you dow huuɓe soɗo?
key_phrases.translation: He, what have you done with your experience so far?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Haa, ɗum ɓurɗo maɓɓe jeyɗi soo lebbi kaw ɗeen ɓurɗo maɓɓe jeyɗi haa kayɗo.
dialogue.translation: Now, my screen is not working very well, but yours is working now, is it good?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Hun, ɗeen goo maɓɓe jeyɗi bii ɗum wooɗiɗi.
dialogue.translation: Here, you can come with me to help me.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ɗum goo kayɗo. Baa kaw ɓurɗo maɓɓe na lewru soo mbii.

dialogue.text: Awa, ɗeen kaaniɓe wiɗa nderɗe haaɓe lebbi.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Palata, ɗum goo haa hun kayɗo bii ɗeen.

scenario: Renting an apartment (first inquiry)
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Pulaar

used to indicate accompaniment or possession

dialogue.speaker: Tenant
dialogue.text: An ñii hun yaw goo hoy ɓurɗo leɗɗe?
dialogue.translation: Do you also have a big room here?

dialogue.speaker: Landlord
dialogue.text: Hun ɗum leɗɗe ɓurɗo goo hoy. Hun haa leɗɗe ɓurɗo bii ɓe?
dialogue.translation: Who has a big room here? Who until has a big room with you?

dialogue.speaker: Tenant
dialogue.text: Mi hoy ɓurɗu leɗɗu goo. Hun lebbiɗo mawnam ɗum ɓurɗo?
dialogue.translation: I have a big room here. What is your price for a big room?

dialogue.speaker: Landlord
dialogue.text: Lebbiɗo ɓurɗu leɗɗu haa ɗiiɓe, mi wonaa lebbiɗo yaw.
dialogue.translation: The price for a big room until next month, I don't have another price too.

dialogue.speaker: Tenant
dialogue.text: Hun, mi heewi lebbiɗo ɓurɗu leɗɗu goo. Haa mi yiɗan.
dialogue.translation: Okay, I agree with the price of the big room here. Until I come.
